newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks seen mixed at open.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks seen mixed at open.

text.p: Wall Street stocks are expected to open mixed Monday after Thursday's 140-point drop in the Dow industrials on fears that rising interest rates could spell the end for the record bull market.
"The foreign markets are all closed so it eases the blow," said Larry Wachtel, analyst at Prudential Securities.
"I don't think we'll have a dramatic downside at the opening. We'll have a mixed start. But the psychology is poor after what happened last week."

February personal income and consumption figures at 0830 EST/1330 GMT will kick off the week with important data, including the March National Association of Purchasing Management index on Tuesday and Friday's March employment data.

As the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond's yield continued to rise above seven percent, analysts said that market players would scrutinize every piece of economic data for an indication as to when the Federal Reserve would move again on interest rates.
In Tokyo, the Nikkei Average ended moderately lower on the last day of the 1996/97 financial year. The average lost 186.32 points, or 1.02 percent, to finish at 18,003.40.
The stock market was closed in London for Easter Monday.
The dollar was trapped in a narrow range in Tokyo and eased back below 1.68 marks, pressured by mark/yen stranegth.
U.S. Treasuries were mostly lower, with the long bond down 4/32 to yield 7.10 percent.

The Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street writes that retail stocks are hot these days but more and more stores are moving to put an end to one of the retail investor's most heavily used tools -- monthly sales figures.
